earlier_scan.source_named: Paradis, Carole. 1983. Description phonologique du guere. Institut de Linguistique Appliquee, Universite d'Abidjan.
earlier_scan.note: Dedicated phonological description exists (Abidjan working paper, not online); language is heavily tonal (10 tones).

sources.citation: Bôle-Richard, Rémy. 2006. Unité et diversité du wɛ de Côte d'Ivoire. Journal of West African Languages 33(2): 109-142.
sources.note: Silent. Comparative phonology of the Wè cluster (Guéré, Wobè, Nidrou; 17 informants, 8 varieties): vowels (§1), consonants (§2, with §2.1 on the Guéré dialects), syllable structure (§3), tones (§4; §4.1 'Le système tonal du guéré', pp. 125-127: 4 level tones H, h, b, B plus rising tones, 6(+2) tonemes in Guéré). The word 'accent' occurs only for tone diacritics (pp. 113, 125); no mention of word stress or prominence.

sources.citation: Singler, John Victor. 1984. On the underlying representation of contour tones in Wobe. Studies in African Linguistics 15(1): 59-75. DOI 10.32473/sal.v15i1.107520
sources.note: Silent. Wobé (Wè Northern) tone reanalysis; quotes Marchese 1979 that Krahn-Guéré-Wobé form 'une seule langue' (p. 59). No occurrence of stress/accent/prominence.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en). 'Guere language' (phonology of the Zagna dialect after Paradis 1983); Wikipedia (fr). 'Guéré (langue)' (bibliography).
sources.note: English page: 10 tones (L, M, H, T and six contours); 'no information about stress or accent'. French page bibliography supplied the Bôle-Richard 2006, Duitsman 1986 and Marchese 1983 references.

sources.citation: Bearth, Thomas & Christa Link. 1980. The tone puzzle of Wobe. Studies in African Linguistics 11(2): 147-207. DOI 10.32473/sal.v11i2.107611
sources.note: Silent. Wobé = Wè Northern (weno1238, ISO wob), the sister variety, not the target. Entire article is on the 14-tone system; 'stress' appears only in the idiom 'we need to stress that' (pp. 168, 175). No stress/accent statement.
